policy: Launch byte check, then one strict routing/tool canary per arm on the canary task, then per decoding seed every arm over all eligible tasks; one harness invocation per task, WORKERS in flight; no efficacy stopping, analysis, submission or training; a failed canary, two excluded rows in one arm, a server restart or 3 h from server-ready stop the generation and keep the completed rows; any other fault stops it without retry

deviations_from_v062_runner: Panel: the DEV14 tasks that the v060 ledger marks ELIGIBLE (gold-pass and empty-fail) at the pin step, in the frozen selection order; the pin step fills the list. NOT_RUN, INCOMPLETE_<stage> and INELIGIBLE_* rows are not eligible and are listed; the pin never waits for them. With fewer than 4 eligible tasks the panel is not run (sentence: fewer than 4 eligible tasks (n_e)). CONFIRM14 is neither read nor listed.

Invocations: one official-entry invocation per task (the per-repository router cannot be shared), WORKERS in flight, each in its own dedicated delegated service with its own memory guard, observer proxy and receipts; a run is the merge of its invocations. The effective budget is the Rich one except concurrency 1 per invocation.

Inputs: the evaluator-only per-repository task file and the v060 rebuild snapshots, given by absolute path. The data directory of the entry is the per_repo directory, which holds no graphs, embeddings or wheels, so the code-graph tools and their prompt section are unavailable on the external tasks (declared confound against the Rich evaluations).

Environment: the Rich serving environment overlaid with the v060 child environment (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, hash and thread settings, router PYTHONPATH). HOME and TMPDIR of an invocation lie below results/extctl_v060/_rebuild/tmp/v070 because the router reaches an owned workspace only below the rebuild root; the directory is removed after the invocation.
Exposure: the evaluator-only task rows (gold patch, FAIL_TO_PASS ids) stay readable by the same user inside the subprocess sandbox, as the Rich task file is.

Admission: the v043 replay receipt (guard mechanics) is required; the v043 gold40 controls receipt is bound to the Rich primary40, and the v060 controls ran without the guard, so no receipt shows that the 4 GiB sandbox cap leaves the external gold runs unchanged. Per-invocation guard receipts record the command and OOM counts.

Arms: three adapters and no base arm (the comparator is the A0mc-ext arm of v068): A_onpol-s1-ext (sft/runs/A1_onpol_v064), A_onpol-s2-ext (sft/runs/A1_onpol_s2_v064) and T_sub-ext (sft/runs/A1_tsub_v064), each pinned by hash and checked against the hash prefix of the pre-registration. The base name and the three LoRA aliases are served by one LoRA-enabled engine of the configuration of v068 (max-loras 3, rank 16). Inside a seed the runs go A_onpol training seed 1, A_onpol training seed 2, T_sub. Training seeds and decoding seeds are different things and are kept apart in ids and tables.

Canary: the first eligible DEV14 task, strict, one per arm with the seed-1 submission, before any run; it is a panel task, so the canary rows are reported separately and never replace panel rows; canary acceptance as in v068 (the literal sentence of the v068 pre-registration), per decision note 97e9f6ee: a canary stops the generation iff it has zero parsed tool calls, a routing fault, or an infrastructure or qualification failure that leaves its row unqualifiable; a row whose error is a normal outcome (a configured budget exhaustion, a context-window error, completion without submit_patch) passes. The result of the v062 canary row check is recorded in the receipt and is not a gate. The failure class is in the stop detail.

Verification: the model inventory is hashed at activation start, at the end and in the preflight; the dependency trees of the eligible environments also after the canaries and after every seed. The verification timeout of the entry is the harness default (300 s, the value of the v060 controls).

Host: preflight and activation (also between runs) refuse while the v060 controls runner is running, because it shares the rebuild root and the CPU and the pinned idle check does not see it. The preflight also runs a router probe: python started in a directory named workspace below the rebuild root with the child environment must find the dependency target of every eligible environment on sys.path.

Housekeeping: the temporary directory of an invocation is removed after its receipt exists; read-only entries are made writable first and a leftover is recorded (tmp-cleanup.json), never fatal. Artifacts must be regular files named after their task; run-level traces/, patches/ and test_outputs/ are hard links.

Exclusion and stops (v070 pre-registration): a panel row is excluded when its invocation fails runner qualification (the checks of qualify_invocation, run on every invocation as it finishes and repeated by every later reader) or its task error lies outside the normal-outcome markers (v056); the exclusion record is written, a receipt that failed qualification is kept inside it, and the generation goes on. A failed canary, the second excluded row of an arm, any server restart (identity of the verified server group and listener; a failed check is repeated once after 2 s) and 3 h from server-ready stop the generation: no new invocation starts, running ones finish, the server is stopped TERM-only and the completed rows are kept and listed (stopped.json). A host-level global OOM, a leaked service cgroup, a controller error (an exception outside RuntimeError, ValueError, KeyError, OSError and SubprocessError) or any other fault stops the generation without a qualifiable record, as in v062.

Comparator: the comparator is v068 attempt 2 (runner r22, generation v068a2), the sole v068 reading; its end marker is completed.json or stopped.json in migration/external-e4b-v068/attempt2/evaluation. The pin step reads the pinned v068 r21 runtime contract (contracts/external-e4b-v068-r21-runtime-PINNED.json, its sha256 recorded) and refuses unless its ledger digest and its eligible list equal those of this pin, so that v070 stops before any rollout. It writes the identity check over exactly the leaves the pre-registration names: ledger digest, eligible list and order, decoding seeds, evaluation budgets, chat_template sha, server_script_sha256, the vLLM, swegemma and harness versions, base model id and LoRA rank. If any leaf differs no A0mc-ext comparator is shown and the differing leaves are listed. --max-loras, --lora-modules and the engine session are excluded from the check and declared as difference (j).

Training-repository overlap: the pin records, per arm, the repository names of its training data (A_onpol: sft/data/onpolicy_v064/A_onpol/manifest.json; T_sub: sft/data/onpolicy_v064/T_sub/manifest.json) against the repositories of the eligible tasks. The table is read exactly (desc.repositories, repository -> trajectory count) and the overlap is listed per arm. The overlap itself is declared and never a stop rule; a manifest that cannot be read, or has no such table, stops the pin before anything is written.

Dependency trees (change record of v068 attempt 2, 3(a) and section 7): a path is left out of the comparison hash of a dependency tree if and only if lstat reports a regular file, its immediate parent directory is named __pycache__ and its name ends in .pyc; everything else is hashed as the v060 tree_hash hashes it. The pin step reads the pinned r22 contract (contracts/external-e4b-v068-r22-runtime-PINNED.json, its sha256 recorded), copies env_tree_sha256 (the admission values) from its eligible rows, recomputes env_tree_filtered_sha256 and refuses unless every environment filtered hash equals the one r22 pinned. Per environment it writes the tree evidence in the form of r22 to migration/external-e4b-v070/env-evidence (pin-tree-<environment>.txt: the exact tree_hash lines; .json: the full, admission and filtered hash and the starting cache list, path, sha256, bytes and mtime_ns of every excluded file) and records their sha256 in pin.tree_evidence, with the cache files that differ from the starting lists of attempt 2 (declared difference (k)). Nothing below an environment tree is created, changed, moved or deleted. The exclusion is not a claim that bytecode caches cannot affect execution.

Feasibility: after the canaries the runner logs a projection of the wall time of the full panel from the server startup and the canary throughput (feasibility.json). It is descriptive and never changes the launch or a stop; the cap of 3 h from server-ready is not a completion guarantee.

Pin: repeatable while no external rollout exists (the v070 server was never launched and no v070 result or invocation log exists; staging or a refused activation that launched nothing does not count); the pin step refuses while the v060 controls runner is running; an earlier pinned file is kept under a superseded name and listed. The pre-registration (b7b4d4be) is a fixed input of the contract. At the pin step the DEV rows of the v060 ledger and the header fields that are checked are copied to contracts/external-e4b-v070-dev-ledger-PINNED.json and its sha256 is pinned in the contract; every later verification, the activation and the analysis included, reads that snapshot and never the live ledger.

Launch order: activation refuses unless the v068 run has ended (completed.json or stopped.json in the v068 evidence directory), besides the host checks of v068. The result freeze of the pre-registration is 2026-11-10 09:00 UTC; the runner only reports it and the analyzer applies it to the reading.

Unchanged from v062: template flag and checks, server script, argv layout, byte-check logic and stop rule (expectation of v066, request model = base name), memory correction and guard, budgets, sampling, seeds, TERM-only cleanup, fail-closed without retry for faults.
